7 انجذم It was, or became, cut off; (S, K;) as also ↓ تجذّم : (K:) [or the latter is said of a number of things; or implies muchness, or frequency:] the two verbs are syn. [respectively] with اِنْقَطَعَ and تَقَطَّعَ. (TA.) ―
-b2- [Hence] you say, انجذم عَنِ الرَّكْبِ (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, cut off from the company of riders upon camels. (TA.) And En-Nábighah says, “صَدَّتْ سُلَيْمَى وَأَمْسَى حَبْلُهَا ٱنْجَذَمَا
” [Suleymà has turned away, and the bond of her union with me has become severed]. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
